title: Hash-Ledger Coordinator for Inter-Request Prefix Sharing and GPU Slot Reclamation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Hot prefix reuse across requests is currently best-effort per-worker which leads to duplicated KV residency across GPU slots and cold-starts on short-lived instances. This increases GPU memory pressure and hurts latency for tail requests. Goal: introduce a lightweight cross-worker 'hash-ledger' coordinator that tracks recent prefix fingerprints and their residency leases across GPUs, enabling safe reclamation of duplicate KV slabs and fast warmup of cold replicas while preserving latency SLOs and multitenancy isolation.

Scope: prototype coordinator service + on-GPU lease metadata; eviction/stealing protocol for reclaiming duplicate prefix slabs; warmup hints for new worker startup; metrics and dashboards; end-to-end correctness tests and gradual rollout. Not in scope: changing model formats, persistent disk-backed KV stores, tenant billing changes.

Design summary: The coordinator maintains a compact in-memory ledger of prefix fingerprints (64-bit XOR-hash, folded) with one-line metadata: tenant_id, model_variant, last_seen_ts, residency_vector (bitset per-GPU-slot shard), ref_hint_count, lease_epoch. Residency is updated via lightweight heartbeats from workers after they materialize a prefix on a GPU slot. Workers consult the ledger before materializing to see whether a compatible slab already exists on another GPU slot in the cluster. If duplication is detected and the latency delta budget allows, the coordinator returns a 'steal' hint enabling a worker to forward requests to the existing slot or to request immediate clone where low-latency is required.

Key behaviors:
- Lease model: workers acquire ephemeral leases (short, e.g., 30s) when they materialize a slab; leases are renewed while traffic persists. Leases enable safe reclamation: when a new worker wants to reuse a slab it can request a lease transfer, and the coordinator mediates to avoid simultaneous evictions.
- Opportunistic reclamation: when memory pressure triggers, coordinator suggests candidates (low ref_hint_count and stale last_seen_ts) for reclamation; worker-side policy performs a final safety check (ongoing decoding KV accesses) before freeing GPU memory.
- Warmup hints: coordinator exposes a ranked warmup list for booting workers (top-N fingerprints per model/tenant with popularity & recency score) so new workers can prefetch the small prefix embedding/KV fragments before receiving first requests.
- Privacy/multi-tenant: ledger keys are namespaced by tenant and model_variant; no raw token/prompt material is ever stored. Fingerprints are non-reversible 64-bit hashes; we add tenant scoping and per-tenant size quotas to avoid cross-tenant leakage or DoS.

Operator and API changes: Add two lightweight API endpoints: POST /ledger/heartbeat (worker -> coordinator) and GET /ledger/query?fingerprint=... (worker queries potential reuse candidates). Both APIs accept compressed binary 64-bit fingerprint and return compact JSON hint objects. Heartbeat frequency defaults to 10s but is tunable per-worker.

Metrics & SLOs: New dashboards and alerts: global_duplication_rate (fraction of materializations suppressed due to reuse), avg_warmup_time_for_new_worker, lease_transfer_failures, on_gpu_mem_saved_mb_by_dedup. Success target: reduce duplicate residency by >= 35% on pilot workloads while preserving p99 latency within 5% of baseline.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in internal dev cluster with read-only query mode (no reclamation) to validate hit rate and warmup lists. 2) Enable lease hints with no-eviction policy and collect telemetry. 3) Gradually enable opportunistic reclamation on low-risk infra (non-critical tenants) with auto-fallback to baseline eviction. 4) Full rollout after 3 weeks of stable telemetry.

Risks and mitigations: network partitions could cause stale ledger state -> we design leases with short TTLs and require workers to verify local KV access before final reclamation. Hash collisions are possible but low probability; to mitigate we include a small secondary fingerprint (e.g., 32-bit slow-check) and require tenant+model match for reuse. Memory overhead of ledger: we use compact arrays and bloom-filter backed sampling for popularity estimation.

Why this is different from earlier efforts: previous tickets focused on aggressive coalescing and compaction on-device. This ticket introduces a cluster-level lightweight coordinator with lease semantics to reduce cross-slot duplication while explicitly supporting warmup workflows and safe reclamation without changing the on-GPU slab allocator internals.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator service implements query and heartbeat endpoints and accepts >2k qps with <5ms median latency under canary load
Workers can consult ledger and suppress duplicate materialization for identified fingerprints in read-only mode
Pilot reduces duplicate GPU-residency for the target model by >=35% compared to baseline on internal dataset
No regression in p99 generation latency >5% during lease-enabled phase for canary tenants
End-to-end integration tests for lease transfer, warmup list generation, and reclamation safety pass in CI

2026-02-20 - Spike complete: measured cross-slot duplication rate on dev cluster (~48%) and median warmup cost (42ms) for new workers
2026-02-27 - Architecture review with infra: agreed on 64-bit fingerprint + tenant scoping; coordinator will be deployed as a stateless-ish service with sharded state in-memory
2026-03-03 - PoC heartbeat API merged (internal PR) and worker SDK stub added; read-only query mode validated in dev cluster
2026-03-09 - Performance bench: coordinator handles 5k qps in our two-node canary; memory footprint estimate is ~120MB for 1M fingerprints after compaction
2026-03-12 - Enabled lease hints in canary cluster with no-eviction; initial telemetry shows 22% duplication suppression (still tuning scoring)
Next: implement opportunistic reclamation safety checks and warmup list ranking adjustments
notes: Follow-up tickets will add tenant quota enforcement, CLI tools to visualize ledger entries, and a sim harness that replays real traffic for validation. Consider adding optional integration with the Console for warmup tuning by model owners.
